Guidance & outlook: Along with the Q1 FY27 financial results, we have released a letter to our shareholders in which we have shared our outlook and have already answered certain pertinent questions about the performance.
So I just wanted to understand the acceleration in LFL growth from 9.2% in 1QFY26 to 45% in 1QFY27.
And therefore, 0.5% in Q4FY26, at 2.5% in Q1FY27, and we believe Q2FY27 will be better than Q1FY27.
Growth & demand: So these 3 structural tailwinds or structural factors are giving us 40%-45% growth rate.
And see, even if you look at Q1FY27 where we grew 2.5% and the corresponding number in the previous year was 11.6%.

So I wanted to extract some more color if possible on this 2.5% growth that you have seen, and we want to see the higher number ahead in context of the 140 bps of price increase that we seem to have taken on an overall basis.
Margins & costs: And while I see several opportunities on gross margin because the scale is still low at 90 stores, logistics cost and conversion cost and buying cost, whatever leverage you get from Domino's, I think still there are opportunities.
One was, just to understand this impact, but I think last quarter you had called out that the ballpark impact of cost inflation was 120 bps, and you've taken sort of a 1% price hike.

And it also indicated the inflation we were seeing on account of the petrol and diesel costs going up, which impacts both in terms of logistics cost for the company and underlying it impacts commodities which we buy because it is an input cost for the vendors that we buy from.
Capex & expansion: And while we commissioned the Mumbai food factory in March and some bit is yet to be commissioned, but from a cash flow standpoint, we are not building such large assets and we have done for up to almost 5,000 stores.
1.5% to 2%, I believe the brand has the capacity to absorb to take forward.
And how does that flow through on to your EBITDA margin expansion target of 200 basis points which were shared earlier.
Balance sheet & cash: We're getting leverage over there as more stores come in, and also, we've driven productivity.
In our analyst meet 15 months back, we had also highlighted one commitment or one goal rather, that we'll go for free cash flow maximization by using dynamic capital allocation.
When you talk about free cash flow maximization, I think over the last 2 years, we did see a dip in free cash flow in FY24-2025, but we did turn around end of FY25.
Risks & challenges: You delivered, fairly healthy gross margins, at 75.5% , despite the headwinds that you talked about in the previous quarter.
So we had explained in the last quarter that we see almost a 200 bps of headwinds on account of costs, which was about 120 bps, like you rightly said on account of LPG.
Since then, and we were looking at about a 70 bps -80 bps headwind.
